I'm sure finishing this game makes me a hacker the same way Star Fox made me a fighter pilot; I’m literally the best around, I’ve just never tried in real life. Hacknet is a simulated hacking tutorial/murder mystery. It’s a bit heavy on the tutorial (I took notes and decimated that learning curve) but the quirky and innovative things this game does with basically text-only interaction made it extremely enjoyable.

Here are some things you should like to nerd out on this game:
-Just you, a black screen and white text, figuring out how the computer needs you to talk to it. (remembering the “help” command is a… help)
-Case Sensitive Typing Tests with Time Limits. (Nailed It!)
-The thrill/panic of a blue screen of death. (…single loud heart beat... Did my actual computer just crash…)

Summary and Details: You, a humble citizen of the internet, are sent an email from Bit, a hacker who is already dead. You must hone your skills to find out his story and give it a proper ending. The randomized quotes from www.bash.org are hilarious throw backs to AIM/ICQ-type chat logs. (Gosh, we were all so witty back then!) There is many a 1337 Easter egg and you get the rear-window voyeurism of looking at peoples’ weird personal files (the internet does not shy away). There were several times I questioned whether or not this was an actual game or if my next “mission” would be to break into “Ambazon” to steal credit card information and post it on the dark web. (That didn’t happen but I wasn’t taking any chances so I turned down the more nefarious hacks.) The summary of my rating and feelings for this game are a solid: “GO! GO! GO!” with accompanying crescendo-ing 80s rock music while I know that my expert typing is literally saving the world.

I'm just going to come right out and say it... This game is amazing, and has earned a spot on the list of games that I will not be uninstalling. It's story is linear, but has enough side-missions to keep you going for a long time, not to mention if you have the expansion "Labyrinths" (which is rollercoaster in of itself). Each main character that you meet will come back at some point in the game, and the personalities are really clear. 

Now for the cons.

There is only one complaint that I have really, and that is the positioning of nodes on the connections space of the workspace. There is no way to alter this, and it can get crouded quite quickly, even covering your own computer connection, so it's essentially luck of the draw. To get around this, I recommend making users until you find a good placement for the first node besides your own computer.

All in all, amazing game. Would play over and over and over again.

The core gameplay of Hacknet revolves around you, a hacker, who can run several different programs to hack into a server and complete some task for a client. For example, hacking into the fried chicken chain CFC server and stealing the list of 11 secret herbs and spices.

It's an interesting concept to start with, however the game falls extremely short in that the gameplay never evolves into anything that is challenging or involves meaningful decision making. 

Hacking each server in the entire game is exactly the same. That is no exaggeration. You literally do the exact same 3-7 things for each server you encounter in order to hack into it. And the worst part about this process is that the "hacking" requires no user interaction. You simply wait 1-2 minutes for the hacking programs to finish, and then you complete whatever task you were assigned to do on the server.

At no point do you need to make any in game decisions when hacking. At no point do you have any decision to make that can affect the gameplay. And that's really where it all falls apart for me. What am I really doing in this game? Because the game really lacks in the feeling of accomplishment.

I can completely understand how this gameplay can appeal to people who want to feel like a hacker, because the game definitely hits the mark in that regard. But once you get past that, you realise there is very little "gameplay" to be had. It just feels like a demo.

I'm sitting here, typing while it's 2:38, listening to the nice beat from Hacknet credits on about a 100-th loop already, forgetting to eat and sleep, really glad I had this deep emotional experience with great music, UX, moral dilemmas, loads of snap decisions, problem solving and a TON of paranoia. It's also a hands on exercise on how NOT to store passwords / use condoms / use encryption =D

This is a really cool game, I don't know anything about real life hacking, but it was a pretty good simulation of poking around a computer in DOS, which is how I imagine hacking to be. The gameplay has you connecting to different computers, stealing, deleting and modifying files to progress the story. Many commands have to be entered manually through the keyboard so there's a lot of typing in this game, which definitely makes it more engaging and its tough under stress! The display is pretty convincing too, its kind of like a Unix thing, with scrolling logs and whatnot. The story's great, you're contacted by a fellow hacker who needs your help and you end up getting wrapped up in a massive corporate cover up involving a dangerous computer program and murder. As good as the story was, I had a little more fun doing the freelance work that leads up to it, it took about 15 hours to beat this game but I feel like I could've played it for 30. The music was the only part I wasn't crazy about, I ended up shutting it off and playing youtube playlists in the background. Although EDM does fit the atmosphere, I think I would've liked more of an ambient soundtrack. I can't really think of another game I've played like it, most "hacking" games are puzzle games, but this is something different entirely. I really liked it, my only gripe is that I wish it was a little longer. But fortunately there is DLC and a great modding community to get many more hours out of it, highly recommended!

[h1]Hacknet[/h1]

Hacknet is a game about hacking as the title might suggest.
I must admit that I have never played anything like this before.

The story was quite interesting and you progress by doing missions that consists of different tasks related to hacking.
You will change information in registries, search for specific information etc. To make this into interesting gameplay you use simple programming to achieve these things when performing hacks. 

As you progress you get access to new "hacking tools" and it becomes less casual. You will sometimes work against a timer while you hack and try to achieve the task at hand. I recommend watching a trailer or in game footage to get a better grasp of what I am talking about, how the hacking progress works.

Sometimes the game can be tricky and you might feel a bit lost. This happened to me on several occasions. 
Luckily there are some guides and helpful pages out there to help you out (Steam forums Reddit etc.).
It is also one of the most satisfying parts of the game; that you are in the dark and never really know how it all will end. 

The soundtrack is really nice. Electronic music while hacking and feeling the pressure of the time running out; it feels [b]intense[/b]!

[h1]To Conclude[/h1]
[list]
[*] Unique interesting game.
[*] Exciting story.
[*] Fantastic electronic music.
[*] Smart interaction of programming.
[*] Great start to learn some programming.
[*] Feels rewarding as you learn some new things and become more independent throughout the game.
[*] - To dumbed down for real hacker enthusiasts.

After playing Uplink back in the day in college, I never really found another hacking simulator that I enjoyed....until Hacknet.  This game is, while it has faults, is definitely now a classic.  

Primarily, the game is a puzzle game that adds interactive fiction, role-playing, non-linear sandbox design, minimal technical skills, and heavy analytical skills (largely needed for the non-linear approaches).  For those that are technical, there may much more linearity but there is still enough guesswork for good exploration.  Ultimately, the game does an excellent job at putting you in the roll of a hacker and while there may be similar commands, the technical pieces are really dumbed down and do get repetitive (a real script kiddie would you know....write scripts).  It is this roleplay that I think the game excels.  I don't want to say too much because that would be spoilerly.

Definitely going to be buying Labryinths.

P.S. Pro-tip: look up how to hack your seetings to use a Grid for your nmap...I learned the trick way too late. :)
